reasons: The rule targets exclusivity binding the Customer; here the only exclusivity architecture (Section 5.8.1) binds Harpoon (Licensor/counterparty) not to develop or license Competing Products in the Territory, and the Section 5.1.3 licence grant is exclusive in AbbVie's (our) favour — exclusivity benefiting Customer is expressly acceptable under the detection guidance.

Section 4.5.1 confers a 'sole right' (not an obligation) on AbbVie to Manufacture and supply, so it is not a requirements or sole-supplier commitment; the deterministic check confirms no such obligation on Customer remains.

Consistent with a compliant finding, the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment is raised, so nothing is over-flagged and the beneficial Harpoon-side exclusivity is preserved.
Rationale accurately cites the supporting provisions and correctly states the clause meets the preferred position (no exclusivity on Customer) rather than merely the fallback.
